skill.name: isometric-animation
skill.description: Create browser-based isometric animations with CSS, SVG, or Three.js. Build layered infographics, extruded blocks, and diagrams that separate and reassemble.
skill.summary: Build isometric web scenes with consistent depth, seekable motion, and a reduced-motion fallback.
skill.author: iart-ai

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown syntax, rendering code, or visual checks. The two CDN imports lack exact version pins, and the screenshot command can run an unpinned package. No evidence of XSS, path traversal, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: The screenshot command can download and run Playwright without a pinned version.
remediation.suggestion: Use a reviewed local Playwright installation pinned by a lockfile, and use the local executable without automatic downloads.

remediation.issue: The GSAP and Three.js recipes execute CDN JavaScript without exact version pins.
remediation.suggestion: Use reviewed local copies or verified bundles with exact versions. Document which examples require network access.

remediation.issue: The instructions describe screenshot and contact sheet helpers that are absent from the package.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the references or include the reviewed helpers. Document a manual screenshot option that does not require fetching tools.

content.user_title: Create Isometric Animations for the Web
content.value_statement: Layered diagrams can be hard to read when angles, shading, and timing vary. Build a browser scene with consistent depth and motion that reveals each layer in order.
actual_capabilities: Choose between true isometric projection and 2:1 dimetric projection for tile and sprite layouts.
Create shaded block faces, projected SVG grids, and staggered layer reveals using CSS or SVG.
Animate layers separating and reassembling, with optional camera drift, parallax, or hover lift.
Set up an orthographic Three.js scene with real geometry, lighting, shadows, and correct depth occlusion.
Use a single timeline or progress value to freeze frames for review.
Show the final assembled state without ongoing motion when reduced motion is preferred.
limitations: The standalone HTML workflow does not export rendered video.
CSS and SVG recipes simulate depth and do not provide true 3D lighting or occlusion.
The CDN-based GSAP and Three.js examples need a network connection unless the dependencies are provided locally.
Headless screenshots require separately available browser tooling. The referenced helper scripts are not included.

use_cases.title: Reveal a product stack
use_cases.description: Show how four product layers fit together by revealing them from the lowest layer to the highest.

use_cases.title: Explain a device assembly
use_cases.description: Separate labeled layers to show their relationship, then animate them back to their assembled positions.

use_cases.title: Prototype an interactive tile map
use_cases.description: Use a 2:1 grid to align tiles and map pointer coordinates back to rows and columns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple layer reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone HTML scene with three CSS layers. Reveal them from bottom to top, and show the assembled state for reduced motion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Create a first isometric scene.

prompt_templates.title: Draw a 2:1 tile grid
prompt_templates.prompt: Draw a 2:1 dimetric grid in inline SVG. Add six shaded blocks and highlight the tile under the pointer.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Add positioning and interaction to a tile map.

prompt_templates.title: Animate an exploded diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate five labeled layers separating and reassembling on one timeline. Keep labels facing the viewer and add frame seeking for screenshots.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Explain how parts fit together.

prompt_templates.title: Build a true 3D stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Three.js scene with an orthographic camera, four stacked blocks, and one directional light. Drive frame seeking and the reduced-motion state from one progress value.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Use real geometry to control shadows and occlusion.

output_examples.input: Make a four-layer stack for a product explainer.
output_examples.output: A browser scene that reveals each layer from the base up. Three paused frames show the start, partial build, and completed stack.

output_examples.input: Show how a device comes apart and fits together.
output_examples.output: An isometric diagram in which labeled parts separate along the vertical axis and return to their seated positions.

output_examples.input: Create a 3D block assembly with visible shadows.
output_examples.output: A Three.js scene with an orthographic camera and directional light. Near blocks hide far blocks correctly without perspective shrink.

best_practices: Choose one projection convention before drawing grids or placing objects.
Keep the light direction fixed and reveal layers in their physical order.
Check the start, middle, and end frames, then verify the reduced-motion state.
anti_patterns: Mixing true isometric axes with 2:1 tiles in the same scene.
Scaling distant objects to suggest height instead of moving them along the depth axis.
Using large camera rotations on a flat CSS or SVG scene.

faq.question: Do I need a build step?
faq.answer: No build step is required for standalone HTML. CDN-based examples still need internet access unless the dependencies are available locally.

faq.question: When should I choose Three.js?
faq.answer: Use it when objects must hide one another correctly, cast real shadows, or rotate in three dimensions.

faq.question: Which projection suits a pixel-art tile map?
faq.answer: Use 2:1 dimetric projection for tiles twice as wide as they are tall.

faq.question: Can I freeze the animation for a screenshot?
faq.answer: Yes. A URL parameter can set the timeline or progress value before the scene renders a still frame.

faq.question: How does the scene handle reduced motion?
faq.answer: The guidance shows the final assembled scene and skips continuous drift and parallax.

faq.question: Does the standalone workflow export video?
faq.answer: No. It produces browser HTML. The skill points to a separate Remotion workflow for video projects.
